scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes local changes in the `Ratio` StructureDefinition from R4 4.0.1 to the R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package. The R6 `StructureDefinition-Ratio.json` is present with the same canonical URL and type, so no rename/removal investigation was needed beyond confirming a related `RatioRange` datatype exists separately in R6. Changes inherited only from `Element`, `DataType`, `Extension`, or from the internal definitions of referenced datatypes such as `Quantity` are not reported as local Ratio findings unless the Ratio element itself changed how it references or constrains that datatype.
outOfScope: The R4-to-R6 baseDefinition shift from `Element` to `DataType` is an inherited datatype hierarchy change, not a local Ratio finding.

Inherited `Element.id`, `Element.extension`, and `Extension` constraint/snapshot differences, including the absence of `ext-1` on R6 inherited extension snapshots, are handled by the Element/Extension analyses.

Internal R4-to-R6 changes in `Quantity`, including the added `ad` comparator code and the R6 `qty-4` best-practice warning, are handled by the Quantity analysis except where Ratio locally narrowed `denominator` to `SimpleQuantity`.
`RatioRange` is a separate R6 datatype and was not treated as a rename, split, or replacement for `Ratio` because `Ratio` remains present with the same canonical URL.

narrativeReportMd:
# Ratio R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
A local hard validation break was found: `Ratio.denominator` is narrowed from general `Quantity` in R4 to `Quantity` profiled as `SimpleQuantity` in R6, which disallows `denominator.comparator`. Existing R4 Ratio instances that used a comparator on the denominator can become invalid in R6.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition/Ratio` snapshots and differentials, then checked `Quantity`, `SimpleQuantity`, and the comparator terminology only to understand the local denominator type-profile change. Inherited datatype hierarchy and Element/Extension changes are out of scope for this report.

## Main migration themes
The instance shape and element names are otherwise stable: `numerator` and `denominator` remain `0..1`, the paired-presence invariant remains semantically equivalent, and no local elements were added, removed, renamed, or moved. The migration work is concentrated on detecting and resolving denominator comparators.

## Highest-impact findings
`Ratio:TYPE_DOMAIN:Ratio.denominator:7681c8` is the only local material finding. The old denominator allowed any valid `Quantity`, including a comparator such as `<`; the R6 denominator points to `SimpleQuantity`, whose constraint and child cardinality require the comparator to be absent.

## Findings requiring human review
Affected records need human or domain-policy review when the comparator changes meaning. Removing `<`, `<=`, `>=`, or `>` from a denominator is not generally lossless, because it can alter the mathematical or clinical interpretation of the ratio.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The change is probably semantically justified because a ratio denominator is normally expected to be a fixed quantity. A less disruptive alternative would have been a warning, profile, or transition-period invariant rather than narrowing the base datatype element.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: One local hard breaking change was found: R6 narrows `Ratio.denominator` to `SimpleQuantity`, so old R4 ratios with `denominator.comparator` are invalid under R6. No local element removals, cardinality changes, reference-target changes, or direct terminology bindings were found. The main uncertainty is rationale rather than the computable delta, because no official diff or ballot rationale was available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should scan all Ratio-valued elements for `denominator.comparator`. If present, systems must decide whether the comparator was erroneous, can be represented elsewhere, or requires manual review. R6-to-R4 local representability is straightforward for valid R6 `Ratio` content because a `SimpleQuantity` denominator is also representable as an R4 `Quantity`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the structural finding because it is directly present in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinition snapshots and confirmed by the R6 `SimpleQuantity` profile. Confidence is lower only for intent and prevalence: the local inputs do not include official change notes or real-world instance statistics.

findings.title: Ratio.denominator narrowed from Quantity to SimpleQuantity

oldState.summary: The denominator element was typed as general Quantity.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `Ratio.denominator` accepted any valid `Quantity`. A denominator `Quantity` could include `comparator` because `Quantity.comparator` had cardinality `0..1` and a required binding to the R4 quantity comparator codes.

newState.summary: The denominator remains Quantity by code but is profiled to SimpleQuantity.

constraints.human: The comparator is not used on a SimpleQuantity

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `Ratio.denominator.type.profile` points to `SimpleQuantity`. The R6 `SimpleQuantity` profile makes `Quantity.comparator` `0..0` and includes the error invariant `sqty-1: comparator.empty()`.

facts.note: The base type code is unchanged, but the R6 type reference adds a constraining profile.
This narrows denominator values to the SimpleQuantity profile.
The profile explicitly rejects any comparator on the denominator Quantity.
The child element is disallowed when the denominator is validated against SimpleQuantity.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are identical (`Ratio.denominator`) in both versions. The only material local type-domain delta is the added `SimpleQuantity` profile on the R6 type reference.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for R4 instances that used a denominator comparator. Such an instance can satisfy R4 `Ratio` because numerator and denominator are both present and the denominator is a valid `Quantity`, but fail R6 validation because the denominator must be a `SimpleQuantity` and `SimpleQuantity` forbids `comparator`. Runtime and code generation risk is medium: generated R6 models or validators may expose/enforce the denominator as a constrained quantity while R4 code may have accepted a full Quantity.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If an approximate or threshold denominator was intentionally used, removing the comparator can change ratio semantics. The affected pattern is probably uncommon, but affected clinical, dosing, laboratory, or rate data should not be normalized blindly.

justification.inferredGoal: Require Ratio denominators to be fixed quantities rather than threshold or approximate quantities.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Ratio.denominator` as base `Quantity` and add a non-fatal best-practice warning plus a stricter SimpleQuantity profile for contexts that require exact denominators.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: a ratio denominator normally represents a fixed divisor, while a `Quantity.comparator` on the denominator can make the ratio a threshold or approximation rather than a precise ratio. Narrowing the base element to `SimpleQuantity` is therefore probably justified, especially because the affected R4 pattern is likely uncommon and may be semantically risky. The verdict is not stronger because the local inputs do not include official rationale, and a less-breaking design could have reduced validation failures at the cost of weaker base semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain the R4 `Quantity` type on `Ratio.denominator`, clarify that denominators are expected to be exact quantities, and add a warning-level invariant such as `denominator.comparator.empty()` while publishing or referencing a stricter profile for use cases that need enforceable exact denominators. That would preserve old R4 instances with denominator comparators, but it would only partially meet the R6 goal: base R6 validators would still accept comparator-bearing denominators, implementations could disagree about whether the warning is actionable, and exact-denominator enforcement would move to profiles rather than the shared base datatype. Migration extensions or conversion tooling for preserving a removed comparator are useful mitigations, but they are not counted as backward-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve R4 denominator comparators but would not provide a base R6 guarantee that every Ratio denominator is exact; profile-only enforcement would create validation variability and weaker interoperability.

evidence.detail: R4 denominator type is `Quantity` with no profile.
R6 denominator type is `Quantity` with profile `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SimpleQuantity`.
R6 SimpleQuantity carries an error invariant requiring the comparator to be absent.
R6 SimpleQuantity sets `Quantity.comparator` maximum cardinality to `0`.
The R4 comparator code system includes comparator codes such as `<`, `<=`, `>=`, and `>` that could be used in an R4 denominator Quantity.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example is a Ratio datatype fragment, not a complete resource. It is R4-valid for the local Ratio rules because both numerator and denominator are present and R4 allowed `Quantity.comparator`; it is R6-invalid because the denominator is now constrained to `SimpleQuantity`. The migration example is illustrative only: no official cross-version extension was identified in the local inputs.

findings.narrativeMd: `Ratio.denominator` was narrowed by adding the `SimpleQuantity` profile. The serialized field name did not change, so the break can be easy to miss in JSON diffs: the same `denominator` object that parsed as a `Quantity` in R4 is now validated as a `SimpleQuantity` in R6. The affected old pattern is a denominator with `comparator`, for example a ratio per `< 1 day` or per `>= 10 mL`. Those old instances become invalid rather than merely semantically discouraged.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid when `denominator.comparator` is present. Valid R6 denominator content is still representable in R4 because `SimpleQuantity` is a constrained form of `Quantity`, so the local R6-to-R4 representability risk is low. Strict validators, generated classes, JSON schema derivations, and business rules that inspect modifier elements may all need updates because the denominator no longer permits the comparator modifier.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan all Ratio-valued data for `denominator.comparator`. If none are present, no transform is needed for this finding. If present, do not simply drop the comparator unless a domain owner confirms it is safe: removal can change the meaning. Potential migration strategies include correcting erroneous source data, moving the original comparator to a documented extension for audit, mapping to a different model that can express a range or threshold, or routing the record for manual review. Regression tests should include Ratio instances with no comparator, comparator on numerator only, comparator on denominator, and denominator omitted/present combinations for `rat-1`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been made less disruptive by retaining `Quantity` on the base `Ratio.denominator` and requiring `SimpleQuantity` only in profiles or through a best-practice warning. That alternative would keep existing R4 data valid but would leave base R6 Ratio with weaker mathematical semantics. The chosen design favors a stronger base guarantee at the cost of rejecting old denominator-comparator instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The structural delta is unambiguous. Human review is recommended for affected instances because the correct remediation depends on why a comparator was used on the denominator.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `Ratio.denominator` to be a general `Quantity`; R6 keeps the same path but constrains it to `SimpleQuantity`. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid break for any R4 ratio whose denominator carried `comparator`. A concrete affected case is ratio-valued clinical or medication data where the denominator was recorded as a threshold or approximate quantity; simply dropping the comparator can change the ratio's meaning, so affected records need domain review. The R6 design goal is understandable because a ratio denominator is normally a fixed divisor, and local package examples did not show this pattern as common. However, this is a hard validation break in a normative R4 datatype, and no local rationale explains why base R6 had to reject the old wire form rather than first using a warning/profile approach. That combination makes the specific path worth renewed standards review.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-Ratio snapshot: `Ratio.denominator` type is `Quantity` with no profile.
R6 StructureDefinition-Ratio snapshot: `Ratio.denominator` type is `Quantity` profiled by `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SimpleQuantity`.
R4 StructureDefinition-Quantity: `Quantity.comparator` is `0..1`, is a modifier, and is required-bound to quantity-comparator.
R6 StructureDefinition-SimpleQuantity: `Quantity.comparator` has max `0` and invariant `sqty-1` has severity `error` with expression `comparator.empty()`.
R4 Ratio metadata and maturity map identify Ratio as normative since 4.0.0.
Targeted local package search found no example `denominator` object containing `comparator`, which tempers prevalence but does not remove the hard-break mechanism.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Ratio is normative, so the stability expectation is high. That raises the justification burden for changing a valid R4 denominator shape into an R6 validation error, especially because comparator is modifier data whose removal can be semantic.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `Ratio.denominator` can legally include `Quantity.comparator`; in R6 the same denominator is validated as `SimpleQuantity`, where comparator is prohibited by max `0` and an error invariant.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design would keep `Ratio.denominator` as `Quantity`, add normative text plus a warning or best-practice invariant discouraging `denominator.comparator`, and publish/use a stricter SimpleQuantity-profiled Ratio where an exact denominator must be enforced. This would preserve old R4 instances but would not provide a universal base R6 guarantee that denominators are exact, so it has real interoperability tradeoffs. Still, for a normative hard break with potentially lossy migration, that tradeoff is credible enough to revisit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing report: the structural hard break and high impact are well supported, and the alternative is only partial because it weakens base enforcement. I am less accepting of the reported 'probably justified' conclusion because the normative status, modifier semantics, and absence of local rationale make this path deserving of renewed review.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, status, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. The baseDefinition change to `DataType` is inherited infrastructure scope.
The local snapshot element ids remain `Ratio`, `Ratio.id`, `Ratio.extension`, `Ratio.numerator`, and `Ratio.denominator`; no local element was added, removed, renamed, or moved.
The root, numerator, and denominator cardinalities remain unchanged. The denominator comparator restriction is represented as a type/profile narrowing and is captured as a finding.
`Ratio` has no Reference-typed local elements, so no reference target comparison applies.
`Ratio` has no direct local terminology binding. Comparator terminology belongs to the referenced `Quantity` datatype; it was checked only to understand the local denominator profile narrowing.

The local `rat-1` invariant was rewritten from an xor form to an explicit paired-presence expression, but the truth table is equivalent: numerator and denominator must either both exist, or both be absent with an extension present. R6 also adds `condition: ["rat-1"]` metadata to numerator and denominator, which points to the same root invariant rather than adding a separate rule.
No local fixed, pattern, or default values were found on `Ratio`, `numerator`, or `denominator` in either version.

No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex restrictions were found on Ratio elements. Child Quantity restrictions are delegated to the Quantity/SimpleQuantity analyses except for the denominator profile change reported here.

`Ratio`, `Ratio.numerator`, and `Ratio.denominator` remain non-modifier elements. The inherited `Quantity.comparator` modifier is relevant only because R6 denominator now disallows it through `SimpleQuantity`.
`Ratio.numerator` and `Ratio.denominator` remain summary elements; inherited `id` and `extension` remain non-summary.
No local slicing was introduced or removed. The inherited open slicing on `Element.extension` is out of scope.

The local short, definition, purpose, and Ratio usage comment are substantively stable. R6 metadata and generated narrative wording changed, but not in a way that changes local Ratio semantics apart from the denominator type profile.
No local JSON/XML element names, choice names, or representation forms changed. The break is validation/profile-based rather than a new serialized shape.

For local Ratio changes, valid R6 denominator content is representable in R4 because `SimpleQuantity` is a subset of `Quantity`. R6-to-R4 risks inherited from internal Quantity changes, such as the added `ad` comparator code on numerator Quantity, are out of scope for this Ratio report.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: rat-1 invariant expression was rewritten but remains equivalent
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 used `(numerator.empty() xor denominator.exists()) and (numerator.exists() or extension.exists())`; R6 uses `(numerator.exists() and denominator.exists()) or (numerator.empty() and denominator.empty() and extension.exists())`. These expressions accept the same local combinations of numerator, denominator, and extension.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validator test suites that assert exact FHIRPath strings may need updates, but instance validation behavior for `rat-1` should not change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds rat-1 condition metadata to numerator and denominator
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added `condition` metadata points to the existing root invariant and does not create a new standalone constraint. It mainly helps tooling show which elements are affected by `rat-1`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or documentation tools that expose ElementDefinition.condition may display new condition references even though the validation rule is not materially new.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 package includes a separate RatioRange datatype
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `StructureDefinition/Ratio` remains present with the same canonical URL and type, so `RatioRange` does not appear to be a replacement or rename for Ratio.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migration work should not map all Ratio values to RatioRange automatically; use RatioRange only where the target R6 element explicitly requires it.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 changes `Ratio.baseDefinition` from `Element` to `DataType`. This inherited datatype hierarchy shift may affect generated class inheritance, but it belongs in the DataType/base infrastructure analysis.

`Ratio.numerator` remains `Quantity`, and `Ratio.denominator` is still a Quantity-derived type. Internal Quantity changes, including comparator terminology changes and new Quantity warnings, should be assessed in the Quantity report.
The Ratio snapshots show inherited extension-content differences between R4 and R6. These are not local Ratio changes and should be handled in Element/Extension-focused reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot rationale was available in the local inputs. The structural delta is clear, but the intended rationale and any recommended migration pattern were inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 change notes, ballot reconciliation items, or a generated R4/R6 diff for `Ratio.denominator`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis used StructureDefinition narrative fragments and computable definitions, not full rendered specification pages or committee discussion.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the rendered R4 and R6 datatype pages and any linked change notes for Ratio.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No live terminology expansion was performed. Local complete CodeSystem resources were sufficient for comparator evidence, but a terminology server would provide independent confirmation.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Expand `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/quantity-comparator` for both package versions with a terminology server.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input package is a ballot build marked not for publication, so details may change before a final R6 release.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final published R6 core package when available.
